newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Four states from 4 continents take "green" initiative.
newsitem.headline: Four states from 4 continents take "green" initiative.

text.p: Germany, South Africa, Brazil and Singapore on Monday launched a joint initiative aimed at overcoming North-South political differences on global warming and energy strategies as well as an umbrella organisation for U.N. environmental bodies,

The four called on this week's Earth Summit of world leaders to send a "clear message" on greenhouse gas emissions that affect climate change. They asked for 15 percent reductions in emissions below 1990 levels by 2010, with a 10 percent reduction by 2005.

The proposal is somewhat stronger than one put forth by the European Union at this week's summit where diplomats have been unable to agree on most targets needed to combat global warming, deforestation and over-consumption of energy.

German Chancellor Helmut Kohl received backing from Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso, South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki and Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong for his proposal for a world environmental centre.

He asked that the United Nations put its myriad agencies and commissions under one roof in a "global environmental umbrella organisation" with the Nairobi-based U.N. Environmental Programme (UNEP) as a "major pillar."
U.N. sources said he had spoken to Secretary-General Kofi Annan about putting such a centre in empty government offices in Bonn. No decision has been taken.
But neither Britain nor the Netherlands thought this was a good idea. "I'm not convinced we need another world organisation," said British Foreign Secretary Robin Cook.

South Africa's Mbeki, however, said the United Nations had a "whole plethora of organisations" dealing with environment, adding: "It is important to see what is to be done so that an effective, concerted effort comes from various organisations"

Cardozo of Brazil told a news conference that "We are not asking for a new organisation. That's not our point." But he said that it was a "good moment to do this" while Annan was working on reforming the structures of the world body.
The four in their statement also:

-- called for a joint strategy for efficient energy, a move away from oil and coal and toward developing solar energy and other renewable forms of power. It said the World Bank should expand programmes in this field and that the decade beginning in the year 2000 should be devoted to this purpose.

-- backed a global conference in Berlin for the year 2000 among leaders of the world's 21 megacities, noting that more than 3 billion people would be living in urban centres by the turn of the century.
-- asked the U.N. Commission on Sustainable Development, set up after the 1992 Earth Summit in Rio de Janeiro, to promote guidelines for public transportation systems.
"We represent four countries on four continents," they said in a statement. "We are the microcosm of the world."
